title: Composition of K-injective-normalized derived comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_i,\mathcal B_i$ for $i=0,1,2$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Assume every complex of each $\mathcal A_i$ admits a K-injective resolution, i.e. a quasi-isomorphism to a complex receiving only null-homotopic maps from acyclic complexes. Let $F_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B_i$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with total right derived functors $(RF_i,\eta^i)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Write $Q_i:K(\mathcal A_i)\to D(\mathcal A_i)$ and $P_i:K(\mathcal B_i)\to D(\mathcal B_i)$ for localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every K-injective resolution $a:N\to I$ put $c^i_a=(\eta^i_I)^{-1}\circ RF_i(Q_i a)$, the canonical resolution identification [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation].

For $0\leq i<j\leq2$ let $r_{ij}:\mathcal A_j\to\mathcal A_i$ and $s_{ij}:\mathcal B_j\to\mathcal B_i$ be exact additive functors, also denoting their termwise derived functors [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Suppose $r_{02}=r_{01}r_{12}$, $s_{02}=s_{01}s_{12}$ and $F_i r_{ij}=s_{ij}F_j$ on objects and morphisms. Use the induced canonical localization identifications throughout.

Suppose natural isomorphisms $\beta_{ij}:RF_i r_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{ij}RF_j$ are given and have the following normalization. For every K-injective $H$ in $\mathcal A_j$ and every K-injective resolution $a:r_{ij}H\to I$ in $\mathcal A_i$, the map $P_i(F_i a)$ is invertible and
$$(s_{ij}\eta^j_H)^{-1}\circ\beta_{ij,Q_jH}\circ(c^i_a)^{-1}=P_i(F_i a)^{-1}.$$
Then for every $L\in D(\mathcal A_2)$,
$$\beta_{02,L}=s_{01}(\beta_{12,L})\circ\beta_{01,r_{12}L}.$$
No $r_{ij}$ is assumed to preserve K-injective complexes.

proof.text: Transport each derived unit from the homotopy-category presentation to a natural transformation on complexes, with component t_F(K):Q(FK)→RF(QK). For every K-injective resolution a:K→I, naturality and cancellation of the invertible unit at I give t_F(K)c_a=Q(Fa). This uses precisely the canonical resolution comparison of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and the Q/Qh identifications of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); elementary naturality and unit pasting argument by T9.

proof.text: For a K-injective H and a resolution a:rH→I, the supplied normalization, multiplied by Q(Fa), c_a, s(c_id) inverse and the target transport, gives t_F(rH) beta_H=target_H s(t_G(H)). The identity-resolution comparison is the inverse of t_G(H), by step 1. For an arbitrary N, choose a resolution u:N→H. Naturality of t_F, t_G, beta and target transports gives the same square after postcomposition with s(RG(Qu)); cancel this isomorphism. Thus the unit square holds at every complex, without requiring rH to be K-injective.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); elementary naturality and unit pasting argument by T9.

proof.text: Form the natural isomorphism gamma by pasting beta01 and s01(beta12), with the prescribed source and target localization composition isomorphisms. The factorization equations for exact functors identify its complex component with beta01 at r12H followed by s01(beta12 at H) and the inverse target composition transport. The target identifications satisfy the same composition equation: degreewise, the strict equalities e01,e12,e02 give equality transports; these compose by proof irrelevance and functors preserve equality transports. Naturality of the localization factors finishes the equation.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); elementary naturality and unit pasting argument by T9.

proof.text: Paste the unit squares of step 2 for beta01 at r12H and beta12 at H. Apply the canonical source/target identities of step 3 and naturality of the target composition isomorphism. This proves that gamma has exactly the same unit square as beta02 at every complex. No K-injective preservation is used.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); elementary naturality and unit pasting argument by T9.

proof.text: For K-injective H choose a:r02H→I. The beta02 normalization makes Q(F0a) invertible. Step 1 expresses t_F0(r02H) as Q(F0a)c_a inverse, so this unit is invertible. Cancel it from the two unit squares in step 4, then cancel the source localization factor. This proves beta02=gamma on QH.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); elementary naturality and unit pasting argument by T9.

proof.text: For any complex N choose a K-injective resolution u:N→H. Naturality of beta02 and gamma and equality on QH give equality on QN by cancellation of the invertible image of Qu under the common target functor. Finally localization natural-transformation extensionality gives equality on every object L of D(A2). Expanding gamma gives exactly the displayed formula.
